# Actual critical-section scale and an open excluded weight region

This is an explicit necessary-condition theorem for the planar proper-A,
zero-B three-cap regime. It uses real K sections and real K sectors,
not just a formal cap-incidence profile. It excludes an open region of
actual section weights; it does not exclude every deficient weight
pattern or resolve (OC).

The mechanism is distinct from the functional obstruction in
`candidate c5a29d6b8953c3ed`.
The latter assigns numerical weights without asserting their realization
by actual critical sections. The present result proves that its stated
weights cannot occur in the small-A bad-source regime.

## 1. Actual hypotheses and exact chord estimates

Let A,K,B be planar convex bodies with (A+B)/2 contained in K, lifted
at the ONLY integer levels -1,0,1. Let y_0 be in int K. Let nonzero
v_1,v_2,v_3 span the plane and satisfy v_1+v_2+v_3=0.
For each i consider the ambient halfspace through (0,y_0) whose B
trace is supporting:

    v_i.(x-y_0)+(v_i.y_0-h_B(v_i))z>=0.

Assume each A and K trace is a proper cut and each displayed ambient
halfspace genuinely ATTAINS the mixed halfspace depth Q at (0,y_0).
The word proper means its boundary line meets the interior of the
body. Write

    a=|A|, k=|K|, b=|B|, M=a+k+b,
    U_i=|A intersect {v_i.x>=2v_i.y_0-h_B(v_i)}|,
    q_i=|K intersect {v_i.x>=v_i.y_0}|,
    U_i+q_i=Q.

The B traces have planar area zero. Define the normalized section
lengths a_i=sigma_Ai>0 and k_i=sigma_Ki>0 at these cuts, and

    s_i=k_i+2a_i, lambda_i=1/s_i,
    Lambda=sum lambda_i, p_i=lambda_i/Lambda,
    t_i=a_i/s_i.

We use the proved actual moment/chord theorem from
`candidate 86934b651b11f7d5`.
It is applicable under exactly the genuine-critical and proper-cut
hypotheses above. It gives k_i>=a_i and the middle-chord center bound

    |c_i|<=a_i(k_i-a_i)/(k_i+2a_i),

where the chord parameter is x=y_0+t Jv_i and J is a quarter turn.
Consequently 0<t_i<=1/3. Its two distances from y_0 along that
parameter obey the stronger exact bounds

    s_i(1-4t_i+6t_i^2)/2 <= each distance
                 <= s_i(1/2-3t_i^2).             (1)

Indeed they are k_i/2 plus or minus c_i; substitute k_i=s_i(1-2t_i)
and a_i=s_i t_i. Since 1-4t+6t^2 decreases from 1 to 1/3 on
[0,1/3], (1) gives in particular

    s_i/6 <= each distance <= s_i/2.              (2)

The upper estimate controls the FAR endpoint too. It is not the
weaker assertion that only the nearer endpoint is at most k_i/2.

For the symmetric core (K-y_0) intersect -(K-y_0), its gauge norm
and the relation sum v_i=0 yield the exact inequality

    p_l/(1-2t_l)
       <=p_i/(1-4t_i+6t_i^2)
                         +p_j/(1-4t_j+6t_j^2)    (3)

for distinct i,j,l, as proved in Section 5 of the functional source.
In particular p_l<3/4: the left side is strictly larger than p_l,
while the right side is at most 3(p_i+p_j).

## 2. A short real chord bounds an entire unique sector

First use canonical coordinates with y_0=0 and

    v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(-1,-1).

Let (0,-beta) be the negative endpoint of the K chord x=0 and
let (rho,-rho) be the positive-x endpoint of the K chord x+y=0.
Both beta and rho are strictly positive. The actual unique sector
for cap 1 is

    Z_1=K intersect {y<0,x+y>0}.

For (x,y) in Z_1 put u=-y>0 and v=x+y>0. The segment joining
(u+v,-u) to (0,-beta) lies in K. It meets x+y=0 at the point
whose x coordinate is beta(u+v)/(beta+v). The fixed endpoint of
that K chord forces this coordinate to be at most rho. Therefore
EVERY point of Z_1 obeys

    beta u+(beta-rho)v<=beta rho.                 (4)

The coordinate change (x,y)->(u,v) has absolute determinant one.
If beta>rho, the positive-quadrant triangle (4) has axis lengths
rho and beta rho/(beta-rho), so

    |Z_1| <= beta rho^2/[2(beta-rho)].             (5)

This contains the whole actual sector, not a selected subtriangle
or a sum of overlapping regions. Boundary lines carry no planar area.

By (2), beta>=1/(6p_1 Lambda) and rho<=1/(2p_3 Lambda).
Thus if p_3>3p_1 then beta>rho, and monotonicity of the right side
of (5) in rho and in 1/beta gives

    |Z_1| Lambda^2 <= 1/[8p_3(p_3-3p_1)].          (6)

One can verify this last substitution directly from
rho^2/[2(1-rho/beta)]; both rho and rho/beta are bounded above by
the stated endpoint estimates. No unsupported separate optimization
of dependent chord parameters is used: upper bounds are applied only
to a function increasing in both of its arguments.

Suppose now that all three middle caps have q_i<=c k for some
c<1/2, and put epsilon=1-2c>0. Since Z_1 is precisely the part
of K missed by caps 2 and 3, inclusion-exclusion gives

    |Z_1|>=k-q_2-q_3>=epsilon k.

Combining with (6) proves the explicit UPPER scale bound

    k Lambda^2 <= 1/[8epsilon p_3(p_3-3p_1)]
                       whenever p_3>3p_1.        (7)

Every permutation is valid: cyclic relabelings give the other choices
of dominant index, and the reflection interchanging x and y gives
the other adjacent sector for each fixed index. That reflection has
absolute determinant one. Thus for a chosen index l and
p_*=min(p_i,p_j), one may use the stronger of the two bounds:

    k Lambda^2 <= 1/[8epsilon p_l(p_l-3p_*)],
                       whenever p_l>3p_*.        (8)

## 3. Determinants and a lower section scale for A

For general v_1,v_2,v_3 as in Section 1, put
D=|det(v_1,v_2)|>0. Translation by y_0 followed by the coordinate
map x->(v_1.x,v_2.x) makes the normals canonical. Its area factor
is D; each normalized section length and each s_i acquires the
same factor D. Therefore Lambda becomes Lambda/D, the weights p_i
and parameters t_i are unchanged, and k Lambda^2 becomes
k Lambda^2/D. Thus the right sides of (7)--(8) are multiplied by
D in the original coordinates. This is the exact determinant
normalization throughout this note.

As proved by the actual two-chord hull argument in Section 5 of the
functional source, for any distinct i,j one has

    a >= (D/2) a_i a_j.

Indeed in the two-normal coordinate plane the cut chords become
one horizontal and one vertical segment. Their convex hull contains
triangles with total area at least half the product of their lengths,
whether or not the two segments intersect. Transforming area back
gives precisely the displayed determinant factor.

If

    p_l>p_i+3p_j and p_l>p_j+3p_i,                 (9)

define the positive numbers

    T_i(p)=[2-sqrt(6p_i/(p_l-3p_j)-2)]/6,
    T_j(p)=[2-sqrt(6p_j/(p_l-3p_i)-2)]/6.          (10)

The arguments of the square roots lie strictly between zero and four:
(9) gives the upper bound, and p_l<3/4 gives the lower bound.
Equation (3), with its other summand at most 3p_j or 3p_i,
respectively, forces t_i>=T_i and t_j>=T_j. Consequently

    a Lambda^2 >= D T_i(p)T_j(p)/(2p_i p_j).       (11)

Conditions (9) also imply p_l>3p_i and p_l>3p_j, so (8) applies.
Combining (8) and (11) yields the genuine common-body inequality

    a/k >= R_epsilon(p),
    R_epsilon(p)=
      4epsilon p_l(p_l-3min(p_i,p_j))
                     T_i(p)T_j(p)/(p_i p_j).      (12)

All quantities refer to the same A and K and the same critical caps.
The determinant cancels exactly. If the cap bounds q_i<c k are
strict, the inequality in (12) is strict as well.

There is also a direct body-mass consequence that needs NO preliminary
cap-fraction or small-A hypothesis. Assume only, in addition to the
actual critical geometry and weight conditions (9),

    Q<=2(a+k+b)/9 and b<=a+k.

Put

    X(p)=4p_l(p_l-3min(p_i,p_j))T_i(p)T_j(p)/(p_i p_j).

Then

    a/k >= X(p)/(9+8X(p)),
    a/b >= X(p)/[9(1+X(p))].                       (12a)

Indeed select the adjacent sector giving the smaller capacity in
(6), and put

    C=D/[8p_l(p_l-3min(p_i,p_j))],
    L=D T_i T_j/(2p_i p_j), so L/C=X(p).

Its actual area is at most C/Lambda^2. On the other hand,

    |Z_i|>=k-q_j-q_l>=k-2Q
      >=k-4(a+k+b)/9>=(k-8a)/9.

These inequalities remain valid even if their last expression is
negative. Thus k Lambda^2<=8a Lambda^2+9C. Since a Lambda^2>=L,
division by a gives k/a<=8+9C/L, proving the first claim. The
second follows from b<=a+k. This is a quantitative lower bound on
the actual endpoint mass; it does not assume a<b/32.

## 4. An explicit open excluded weight region in the small-A branch

Assume additionally the actual bad-source and area conditions

    Q<=2(a+k+b)/9, b<=a+k, a<b/32.                (13)

No assumption that Q is the global mixed maximum is needed here;
the genuine depth-critical premise at the specified source remains
necessary for Section 1. The last condition is available in the
previously proved two-positive-residual branch; it is kept explicit.

Equations (13) imply

    a/k<1/31,
    q_i<=Q<=4(a+k)/9 <(128/279)k.

Thus use epsilon=23/279 in (12). Define the following open region
of the probability simplex, and allow every permutation of its indices:

    p_i,p_j,p_l>0, sum p=1, p_l<3/4,
    p_l>p_i+3p_j, p_l>p_j+3p_i,
    R_(23/279)(p)>1/31.                            (14)

Every actual critical weight vector satisfying (13) lies OUTSIDE
this region. This follows immediately by combining (12) with
a/k<1/31. Formula (14) is explicit, continuous, and algebraic
with specified nonnegative square roots, so it is an open sufficient
exclusion region. No assertion that it is the full excluded set is
made.

Equivalently, its final condition is the particularly simple

    X(p)>9/23.

This follows because R_(23/279)=(23/279)X and 279=9*31.
The same exclusion follows directly from (12a): X>9/23 gives
a/b>1/32.

In particular, the originally assigned weights

    (p_i,p_j,p_l)=(7/50,7/50,18/25)

are excluded by a wide exact margin. Equations (10)--(12) give

    T_i=T_j=(1-1/sqrt(5))/3,
    a Lambda^2/D >=(1500-500sqrt(5))/441,
    k Lambda^2/D <3875/552,
    a/k >736(3-sqrt(5))/4557 >1/31.               (15)

For the final comparison, sqrt(5)<5/2 gives
736(3-sqrt(5))>368>147 and 4557=31*147.
Thus the coarse functional obstruction cannot be realized by the
actual critical sections in this small-A branch.

For these specific weights, X=96(3-sqrt(5))/49. Even without
assuming the small-A condition, (12a) forces a/b>1/16: use
sqrt(5)<9/4 to obtain X>72/49>9/7, and
X/[9(1+X)]>1/16 is exactly X>9/7.

A simple OPEN RECTANGLE inside (14) is

    13/100<p_i<3/20, 13/100<p_j<3/20,
    p_l=1-p_i-p_j.                                (16)

Indeed 7/10<p_l<37/50<3/4, and both inequalities (9) hold.
Moreover p_i/(p_l-3p_j)<(3/20)/(1/4)=3/5,
and symmetrically. Since sqrt(8/5)<32/25, (10) gives
T_i,T_j>3/25. Also p_l(p_l-3p_*)>(7/10)(1/4)=7/40
and p_i p_j<9/400. Therefore

    R_(23/279)(p)
       > (56/125)(23/279)=1288/34875>1/31,

the last comparison being 31*1288=39928>34875. This proves an
explicit nonsymmetric neighborhood, not only the isolated weight.

## 5. The whole symmetric heavy-weight interval

For p_i=p_j=(1-P)/2 and 2/3<P<3/4, equations (10)--(12) simplify to

    R_(23/279)(p)=
      [8epsilon P(5P-3)/(9(1-P)^2)]
        [1-sqrt((3-4P)/(5P-3))]^2,
      epsilon=23/279.                              (17)

Every factor on the right increases with P on this interval:
P increases; (5P-3)/(1-P)^2 has derivative
(5P-1)/(1-P)^3>0; and (3-4P)/(5P-3) has derivative
-3/(5P-3)^2<0. At P=7/10 its square-root term is sqrt(2/5).
Using sqrt(2/5)<19/30 gives

    R_(23/279)(p)
       > [280epsilon/81]*(11/30)^2
       = (1694/3645)epsilon >1/31.

For the last comparison, with epsilon=23/279,
31*1694*23=1207822>3645*279=1016955.
Therefore every symmetric vector with 7/10<=P<3/4 is excluded
under the actual hypotheses (13). The endpoint P=3/4 is already
impossible for proper A cuts by the strict observation after (3).

There is also a useful nonsymmetric strip reaching highly unequal
smaller weights. Under (13), it is impossible to have

    p_i<=2/9, p_j<=2/9, 11/15<=P=p_l<3/4.         (18)

To prove it, write p_i=1-P-p_j. The function

    p_i/(P-3p_j)=(1-P-p_j)/(P-3p_j)

increases with p_j, since its derivative in p_j has numerator
3-4P>0. For p_j<=2/9 it decreases with P, since its derivative
in P has numerator 4p_j-1<0. The denominator is positive throughout
(18). Its maximum is therefore at P=11/15,p_j=2/9, and equals
(2/45)/(1/15)=2/3. The symmetric ratio obeys the same bound.
In particular (9) holds and (10) gives

    T_i,T_j>2/21,

using sqrt(2)<10/7. Furthermore

    P-3min(p_i,p_j)>=(5P-3)/2>=1/3,
    p_i p_j<=(1-P)^2/4<=4/225.

Consequently

    X(p)>4*(11/15)*(1/3)*(2/21)^2/(4/225)
         =220/441>9/23,

where the last strict comparison is 5060>3969. This proves (18)
from the open criterion. In particular it applies whenever both
smaller singleton loads are deficient and r<=2/9, since those
weights are then below 2/9. No assertion is made for a pattern with
only one deficient singleton weight.

The present result is a quantitative actual-scale restriction. It
does not convert one-cover stationarity into full extremality, does
not assert that every bad source has weights in (14), and does not
assume that all formal incidence profiles are geometrically critical.
